# docker_plugin

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: resource. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

A managed Docker Engine plugin installed from a registry, like `docker plugin install`. The privileges the plugin asks for (`GET /plugins/privileges`) must be granted with `grant_all_permissions` or `grant_permissions` blocks, otherwise install fails and lists them. `enabled` and `env` change in place (the plugin is disabled for `PluginSet` and re-enabled). With `alias` set, a changed `name` upgrades the plugin in place (`docker plugin upgrade`: disable, `PluginUpgrade`, re-enable), keeping its local name and settings; without `alias`, a changed `name` forces a new resource, since the local name is derived from it. A changed `alias` always forces a new resource. Import by plugin ID or name.

### `grant_permissions`

set of blocks. Privileges to grant, one block per privilege name, e.g. `name = "network"`, `value = ["host"]`. Install fails when the plugin asks for a privilege or value not listed. Conflicts with `grant_all_permissions`. Changing it does not reinstall the plugin.

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required |  |  | Privilege name, e.g. `network`, `mount`, `device`, `capabilities`. |
| `value` | `set(string)` | required |  |  | Granted values, e.g. `["host"]` for `network` or `["CAP_SYS_ADMIN"]` for `capabilities`. |

## Example

```terraform
# With alias set, changing name later upgrades the plugin in place
# (docker plugin upgrade) instead of replacing it.
resource "docker_plugin" "sshfs" {
  name  = "vieux/sshfs:latest"
  alias = "sshfs"

  # The privileges the plugin requests; install fails if one is missing.
  grant_permissions {
    name  = "network"
    value = ["host"]
  }
  grant_permissions {
    name  = "mount"
    value = ["/var/lib/docker/plugins/"]
  }
  grant_permissions {
    name  = "device"
    value = ["/dev/fuse"]
  }
  grant_permissions {
    name  = "capabilities"
    value = ["CAP_SYS_ADMIN"]
  }

  env            = ["DEBUG=1"]
  enabled        = true
  enable_timeout = 120
}

resource "docker_volume" "remote" {
  name   = "remote-data"
  driver = docker_plugin.sshfs.alias
  driver_opts = {
    sshcmd = "user@files.example.com:/srv/data"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
# Import by plugin ID or name.
terraform import docker_plugin.sshfs sshfs:latest
```
